# Fovea

A color scheme informed by vision research: three variants built from one OKLCH palette, each checked against a contrast budget.

![Fovea Day: an editor window with code drawn as colored bars](https://github.com/natewave/fovea/raw/HEAD/docs/assets/preview-day.png)

![Fovea Dusk: an editor window with code drawn as colored bars](https://github.com/natewave/fovea/raw/HEAD/docs/assets/preview-dusk.png)

![Fovea Night: an editor window with code drawn as colored bars](https://github.com/natewave/fovea/raw/HEAD/docs/assets/preview-night.png)

Fovea designs lightness first and hue second. The center of the fovea, the part of the eye that
reads, has no blue-sensitive cones, so text is resolved by lightness contrast. Every text color
clears a contrast floor on every surface it can sit on, red is kept for errors and deletions,
and the chrome around the editor stays quiet so the code is the sharpest thing on screen.

| Variant         | Made for                                                                                                           | Text contrast (perceptual contrast (Lc) · WCAG) |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| **Fovea Day**   | Ink on warm paper. The most legible variant for long reading, and the natural match for bright rooms and daylight. | Lc 96 · 14.1:1                                  |
| **Fovea Dusk**  | Soft light on warm graphite, for dim rooms, evenings and anyone who prefers dark mode.                             | Lc 87 · 13.2:1                                  |
| **Fovea Night** | Dusk dimmed for dark rooms and late hours: the least light that still meets body-text minimums.                    | Lc 78 · 12.5:1                                  |

A color theme can't prevent eye strain or improve sleep. Screen brightness, room lighting and
breaks matter far more. The website's [science page](https://natewave.github.io/fovea/science/) explains what
the evidence does and doesn't support.

## Install

Fovea isn't on the Visual Studio Marketplace or Open VSX yet. Until it is, install it
from source:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/natewave/fovea.git
cd fovea
pnpm install
pnpm package:vscode
code --install-extension dist/vscode/fovea.vsix
```

In Cursor, use `cursor`; in VSCodium, use `codium` instead of `code`.

Then open the Command Palette, run **Preferences: Color Theme** and pick **Fovea Day**, **Fovea Dusk** or **Fovea Night**.

## Recommended settings

Follow your system's light or dark appearance:

```json
{
  "window.autoDetectColorScheme": true,
  "workbench.preferredLightColorTheme": "Fovea Day",
  "workbench.preferredDarkColorTheme": "Fovea Dusk"
}
```

Fovea Day is the most legible variant for long reading. Studies of reading on screens
found dark text on a light background read more accurately, and the gap was largest in dark
rooms. Fovea Dusk and Fovea Night are for dim rooms and personal preference. In
a dark room, Fovea Night emits the least light; switch to it with:

```json
{
  "workbench.preferredDarkColorTheme": "Fovea Night"
}
```

See [the settings docs](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/themes#_automatically-switch-based-on-os-color-scheme).

## Italics

Fovea uses no italics: the British Dyslexia Association's style guide advises against them. To
italicize comments, add this to your settings. A rule that sets only a font style keeps Fovea's
colors.

```json
{
  "editor.tokenColorCustomizations": {
    "[Fovea*]": {
      "textMateRules": [
        {
          "scope": [
            "comment",
            "punctuation.definition.comment"
          ],
          "settings": {
            "fontStyle": "italic"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## Bracket pair colors

Brackets are punctuation, so Fovea draws every bracket pair in the punctuation color. To bring
back VS Code's colors for nested pairs (they are not part of Fovea's contrast checks):

```json
{
  "workbench.colorCustomizations": {
    "[Fovea*]": {
      "editorBracketHighlight.foreground1": "default",
      "editorBracketHighlight.foreground2": "default",
      "editorBracketHighlight.foreground3": "default",
      "editorBracketHighlight.foreground4": "default",
      "editorBracketHighlight.foreground5": "default",
      "editorBracketHighlight.foreground6": "default"
    }
  }
}
```

## How Fovea is checked

Every color is generated from one palette and checked by automated tests: text contrast on
every background it can appear on, color-vision deficiency simulations for semantic pairs such
as added and removed lines, and coverage of VS Code's theme color reference. The
[design notes](https://github.com/natewave/fovea/blob/HEAD/docs/design.md) give the method and the numbers.
